info.description:
The Power Platform API is Microsoft's documented control plane for Power Platform administration, organised into namespaces — environment management, licensing, governance, connectivity, app management, Power Pages, Copilot Studio, analytics and more.

Requests carry an `api-version` query parameter. Its accepted values are not uniform across the API: some routes take an ordinal such as `1` or `3`, others a dated version such as `2024-10-01` or `2021-10-01-preview`, and several accept more than one. Send the value the operation declares. Alongside the global host, some operations are addressed on **tenant-scoped** (`{tenantId}.tenant.api.powerplatform.com`) or **environment-scoped** (`{environmentId}.environment.api.powerplatform.com`) hosts, where the host itself identifies the scope and the path carries no id.

Unofficial and reverse-engineered — see the [README](https://github.com/AdamCoulterOz/powerplatform-apis/tree/main/ppapi) for how it was derived and which parts are verified.

notes.note: Sending a junk *ordinal* `api-version` makes the gateway enumerate that resource's own accepted ordinals in the error message, which is how the per-route sets here were derived rather than inferred. Across the 43 parameterless GET routes, 33 resolve and **32 of them accept only ordinal `1`**; `/powerapps/notifications` is the sole exception, accepting `1` and `3`. The dated versions are validated separately at the gateway and are not enumerated per resource, so a route's ordinal set is not its complete set.

Ten environment mutation operations return an undocumented **409** carrying `ValidationResponse` -- `provisioning/environments` and, on an environment, `enableDisasterRecovery`, `failback`, `forceFailover`, `governanceSetting/enableManaged`, `governanceSetting/disableManaged`, `modifySku`, `recover`, `reset` and `restore`. Microsoft's own client handles that status on all ten; the published reference documents it on none. A conflicting concurrent operation is the expected cause, so a client that treats 409 as an unexpected failure will mishandle the ordinary case.

Scoped hosts are built by **splitting the last characters of the id into their own DNS label**, not by a fixed 30/2 offset: strip the dashes, take the final two characters as one label and everything before them as the label in front. For a 32-character GUID that reads as 30+2, but the rule is positional from the end, so a non-GUID environment id keeps its prefix intact -- `Default3496a85439b341bda7831f2479ca3fbd` becomes `Default3496a85439b341bda7831f2479ca3f.bd.environment...`.

**The count is not two in every cloud.** Microsoft's own enterprise-policies module splits off only **one** character for the tip1 and tip2 test rings and for usgovhigh and dod. So two first-party samples that appear to contradict each other on 30+2 versus 31+1 are each correct for the cloud they target, and a client that hardcodes either number is wrong somewhere.

Confirmed live for the commercial cloud: the two-character form resolves through a CNAME to a regional gateway and answers `401` without a token, while the one-character form is NXDOMAIN. The sovereign counts are from the module's source and have not been observed. Note how the wrong split fails -- DNS resolution, not an API error -- which sends whoever debugs it to networking rather than to the hostname.

**PPEM -- Power Platform Environment Management -- is replacing BAPI's environment lifecycle, one operation at a time, behind feature flags.** The admin centre carries both implementations and chooses between them per operation at runtime. The flags found in its configuration, each swapping one call from the legacy BAP route to a PPEM one: `UsePpemBackupApis`, `UsePpemCopyApi`, `UsePpemRestoreApi`, `UsePpemRecoverApi`, `UsePpemResetApi`, `UsePpemDeleteApi`, `UsePpemFailoverApi`, `UsePpemProvisioningApi` (which moves even the locations, currencies and languages reference data), `UsePpemGetLifecycleOperationsApi`, `UsePpemGetLifecycleOperationByIdApi`, and `UsePpemManagedEnvironmentApis`.

Two consequences worth planning around. The same logical operation has two live implementations with **differently shaped bodies** -- the reset flag's own description notes PPEM's takes a different shape from BAP's. And because every flag was off in the tenant observed, the module that builds the PPEM URLs never loaded, so the request shapes and enums are recoverable from the bundle but the paths are not. This is surface that demonstrably exists and could not be captured.

**Internal service codenames**, recovered from the admin centre's own code. They are worth recording because they explain otherwise-unexplained names in this spec and in error payloads.

**Neptune** -- licensing; also appears as the `x-ms-neptune-environment-id` request header, and explains the `Neptune*` schemas here.
**Quartz** -- the rule-set and rule-based-policy engine behind `/governance/`.
**Artemis** -- the environment-scoped settings store behind `/environmentmanagement/environments/{id}/settings`, which returns a non-ARM `{objectResult:[...]}` envelope rather than the usual shape.
**Cafe** -- the per-setting Copilot governance store behind `/copilotgovernance/`.
**PPEM** -- the replacement environment-lifecycle service described above.
**PARP** -- the PowerApps Resource Provider, the legacy `/providers/Microsoft.PowerApps/` surface that PPAPI supersedes; the client sends `x-ms-deprecate-legacy-parp` when it wants the new path.
**Apollo** -- solutions and diagnostics. **Kepler** -- a first-party Entra application whose consent the user-management surface requires in test rings. **DAC** -- the admin centre application itself. **Centro** -- the Microsoft 365 admin centre.

**The admin centre's bundles do not contain hostnames at their call sites.** Requests are built against sentinel service names -- `bap-rp`, `pa-rp`, `flow`, `flowV2`, `ppapi`, `ppapi-tenant-level`, `ppapi-pauto`, `ppac-rp` -- and an interceptor swaps each for the real endpoint registered for that service in the current ring. Anyone reading these bundles must resolve the sentinel before attributing a route to a host, and the `il-` prefix marks the tenant-island variant of the tenant-level host rather than a different service.

Also present: a 128-entry table mapping every legacy `/providers/Microsoft.PowerApps/...` path onto its PPAPI successor, with the namespace each lands in. It is the migration map between the two surfaces, and it is the reason both appear in this corpus.

**What was found in the bundles and deliberately not modelled here.** The mining produced 522 candidate operations; 95 are modelled across this corpus. The rest failed one of two bars and are recorded as a count rather than as entries:

- **294 had no determinable HTTP method.** Minification separates the path literal from the call that uses it, and a guessed method is worse than none -- a spec that says GET where the service wants POST sends a reader somewhere a missing entry would not.
- **104 were assembled from concatenated fragments** rather than appearing as a whole string. The segments are real; their order and separators are inferred.

By namespace the unmodelled remainder is heaviest in `/analytics`, `/governance` and the PowerApps legacy surface. A capture of the corresponding admin-centre pages would settle the methods for most of them, since a recorded call carries the method the bundle does not.

**Status codes on the environment lifecycle are specific and not interchangeable**, asserted exactly by a first-party client's live-run tests rather than inferred: a real environment delete returns **202** with an `operation-location` header; creating a backup returns **201**; deleting a backup returns **204**; provisioning a new environment returns **201** when it completes synchronously and **202** when it does not; executing disaster recovery and running a DR drill each return **201** rather than the 202 an async operation would suggest; and enabling or disabling DR returns **202**, with both supporting `ValidateOnly`. A client that accepts any 2xx will work; one that switches on the exact code needs these.

**Two independent clients disagree on the BAP token scope, and one of them has a double slash**: `https://service.powerapps.com//.default` against `https://service.powerapps.com/.default`. Both are in shipped code from separate vendors. A doubled slash in a scope is the kind of thing that is copied forward for years because it happens to work, so a client seeing an unexpected token audience should check this before looking anywhere else.

**A `403` on this API is as much a fact about the principal as about the route, and the asymmetry runs both ways.** The same sweep, as an interactive user and as a service principal:

Readable only by the **service principal** -- `analytics/advisorRecommendations`, `powerapps/apps`, `powerapps/environments`, `powerapps/notifications`: `403` as a user, `200` as an SP.

Readable only by the **user** -- `authorization/roleAssignments`, `authorization/roleDefinitions`, `environmentmanagement/environmentGroups`, `environmentmanagement/provisioning/locations`, `governance/ruleBasedPolicies`, `governance/ruleSets`, `licensing/FinOpsLicensing/GetLicenseSummaryV2`: `200` as a user, `403` as an SP.

**Neither principal is a superset of the other**, so there is no single identity that can read this API completely. Two separate mechanisms are at work and the sweep separates them cleanly: route *existence* is not principal-dependent at all, while route *authorization* strongly is. Any evidence recorded here that rests on a status code needs the principal recorded alongside it, per capture rather than per evidence set.

**Host affinity is per route, not per namespace.** `environmentmanagement/environments` answers `200` on the shared `api.powerplatform.com` host and `400 EndpointInvalid` on the tenant-specific `{id}.{realm}.tenant.api.powerplatform.com` host -- for both principals. `environmentmanagement/provisioning/locations` works on either. So a client cannot pick a host per namespace and use it throughout, and anything migrating environment reads onto a tenant-host helper will fail on a route that looks like it should work.

**Twelve documented routes do not resolve, and the cause is not the caller.** All 51 parameterless GET routes were swept twice against `api.powerplatform.com` at `2024-10-01` -- once as an interactive user and once as an app-only service principal -- and **every `RouteNotFound` was identical across both**. Not one flipped. Principal type is therefore eliminated, leaving three candidates: a licence gate, a tenant feature flag, or a gateway older than the documentation.

`/analytics/advisor/chat/conversations`, `/governance/lockboxPolicies`, `/governance/tenantRuleBasedPolicies`, `/notificationservice/notifications`, `/notificationservice/notifications/metadata`, `/powerapps/environment`, `/powerapps/features`, `/powerapps/globalApps`, `/powerapps/plans`, `/workflowsagent/conversationTranscripts`, and `/environmentmanagement/provisioning/create` -- which is documented with the same request body as the primary provisioning route and simply is not there.

**The sweep returned sixteen, and four of them are explained rather than unexplained.** The four `plex` diagnostics answer `404` on the shared host because they do not live there: three are on the environment-scoped host and `networkUsage/subnetHistoricalUsage` is on the tenant-island host. Asking the wrong address returns the same status as a route that does not exist, which is the sharpest illustration of this API's per-route host affinity -- a sweep cannot distinguish 'absent' from 'elsewhere' without knowing the host in advance.

`/connectivity/connections` and `/connectivity/connectors` were explained the same way earlier: they exist on the environment host and the published reference gives the global one.

servers.description: Global endpoint. Every documented operation is reachable here; the gateway routes the request to the tenant's own cluster. First-party clients use it for operations that are not already scoped to one tenant or environment by the caller's context.

Tenant-scoped endpoint. The host is derived from the tenant id alone — there is no region or scale-unit in it. Remove the hyphens from the tenant id to get 32 hex characters, then split: the first 30 are the first DNS label and the remaining 2 are the second. Tenant `00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ab` therefore resolves to `https://000000000000000000000000000000.ab.tenant.api.powerplatform.com`. Operations served only here act on the calling user or the tenant as a whole and take no tenant id in the path.

tenantIdTail.description: The last 2 characters of the tenant id with its hyphens removed.

servers.description: Environment-scoped endpoint. Built from the environment id by the same rule as the tenant host: strip the hyphens to get 32 hex characters, take the first 30 as the first DNS label and the last 2 as the second. Environment `00000000-0000-0000-0000-0000000000ab` resolves to `https://000000000000000000000000000000.ab.environment.api.powerplatform.com`. The environment is implied by the host, so these paths carry no `/environments/{environmentId}` segment — `/connectivity/connections` here is the same resource as `/connectivity/environments/{environmentId}/connections` on the global host.

Microsoft Entra ID OAuth2. The audience is `https://api.powerplatform.com` for all three hosts — the tenant- and environment-scoped hosts take the same token as the global one, so there is nothing per-host to acquire.

Requesting `.default` yields whatever delegated permissions the client application has been granted; `x-delegated-scopes` lists the granular delegated permissions this API defines. Operations do not publish which of those scopes they require individually.

Advisor Chat.description: A conversational assistant that answers questions about the tenant in prose, backed by whatever the service knows about it. Separate from the advisor recommendations in the same namespace, which return structured findings against specific resources, and from the solution-checker advisor on another host entirely. Preview: the surface is feature-gated in the only client known to call it.

Cluster.description: The regional service cluster that serves a tenant or an environment. Its name appears in the `x-ms-gateway-clusters` response header on every call and identifies which stamp, geography and release ring the caller is talking to.

Copilot Governance Setting.description: A single tenant- or environment-level consent switch for a generative AI capability — typically whether a named model provider may be used as a subprocessor. Each setting carries its own admin-centre presentation, the rule that backs it and the effective value.

Feature Gate.description: A named feature flag as evaluated for the caller or the environment. Read-only: the platform decides the value and reports where it came from.

Governance Configuration.description: Tenant-authored governance content surfaced to makers in the maker portal, addressed by configuration name.

Notification.description: In-product notifications for the calling maker, and the Web PubSub channel that pushes them live.

Service Plan.description: The Power Platform service plans (licences) assigned to the calling user, and the policy limits each plan grants.

User Setting.description: A per-user preference blob stored against the caller's Entra object id and addressed by setting name. The maker portal uses them to persist UI state; each setting name has its own free-form shape.

Network Diagnostics.description: Diagnostics that run **from inside an environment's injected subnet** rather than from the caller. That is what makes them useful: they answer what the environment can reach, which no request made from outside it can establish.

Tenant Analytics.description: Tenant-wide analytics and the admin actions the analytics experience can trigger, including the security responses behind attacker-IP blocking.

Application Management.description: Installing and tracking application packages in an environment.

Connectivity.description: Connectors and connections, and the permissions attached to them.

Copilot Governance.description: Per-setting Copilot governance, whose backing store the client calls *Cafe*. Settings are addressed individually by name rather than as one document.

Dynamics.description: Dynamics-specific surfaces exposed through the Power Platform API.

Power Apps (PPAPI).description: Power Apps resources addressed through the Power Platform API rather than the legacy PowerApps resource provider.

Power Automate (PPAPI).description: Power Automate resources addressed through the Power Platform API.

Governance.description: Rule-based policies, lockbox, tenant isolation and the policy engine internally called *Quartz*.

Licensing (PPAPI).description: Licensing surfaces addressed on the Power Platform API host rather than the licensing host.

Support.description: Support tooling the admin centre calls on the tenant's behalf.

Notifications.description: Admin notifications raised to the tenant.

notes.note: The write is optimistic: it can answer 409 or 412, neither of which the published reference documents. A caller that ignores them will silently lose an update.

On a tenant that selects locations by geo, the response carries `collection` only: `macroRegions` and `locationSelectionMode` are absent from the body entirely rather than present and null. A client must treat both as optional keys, not as nullable fields. What the response looks like on a tenant that selects by macro region has not been observed by anyone, and the accepted `macroRegionId` values are published nowhere -- not in the reference, and not in any first-party client.

`api-version` has two independent axes and the documented ordinals are real. `api-version=1` returns 200 on this route, byte-identical to `2024-10-01`. A junk *date* is refused by the gateway with a message listing the four dated versions; a junk *ordinal* is refused with a nested `ApiVersionUnsupportedForResource` and a message listing that resource's ordinals. So the dated list is the gateway's set and says nothing about any single resource, and `info.x-api-versions` is a union across resources rather than a set every route accepts.

An api-version rejection does not return the documented `ValidationResponse`. It returns the gateway's own envelope -- `code`, `message`, nested `innererror` -- so a client that parses 400s according to this operation's documented schema will fail on the most likely 400 it will ever see. Whether the resource itself returns `ValidationResponse` for its own validation failures has not been observed.

Asks the Power Platform advisor a question about the tenant and returns its answer. Omit `conversationId` to start a new conversation; the response carries the id the service assigned, and passing it back on the next request continues the same thread with its history intact. This is not the solution-checker advisor at `advisor.powerapps.com`, and it is unrelated to the advisor recommendations elsewhere in this namespace: those return structured findings about resources, this returns prose.

EnvironmentManagementSetting.description:
One environment's management settings, one property per setting.

Every property name is PascalCase on the wire — `Id`, `PowerApps_AllowCodeApps` — and `$select` matches it case-sensitively. The names below are the wire spelling.

A setting that has never been set is returned as an explicit `null`.

Id.description: The environment id. Always returned, whatever `$select` asks for.

PowerApps_AllowCodeApps.description: Whether makers may run code apps — apps authored outside Power Apps and brought in to run on the platform. Turning it off stops existing code apps running. `null` until the setting has ever been set.

PowerApps_EnableGenerativePages.description: Whether generative pages may be created in this environment. Absent from the published reference; accepted by `$select`.

CopilotStudio_ComputerUseEnabled.description: Whether Copilot Studio agents may use computer use — driving another system's graphical interface with a vision model. Named as a rule input by the rule-set UI configuration; absent from the docs.

CopilotStudio_ComputerUseDedicatedMachin.description: Whether computer use may run on machines dedicated to this tenant. Named as a rule input by the rule-set UI configuration; absent from the docs.

CopilotStudio_ComputerUseByoMachines.description: Whether computer use may run on machines the customer brings. Named as a rule input by the rule-set UI configuration; absent from the docs.

CopilotStudio_ExternalModels.description: Whether makers may build on non-Microsoft models in Copilot Studio. Backs the per-provider consent switches under [Copilot Governance Setting](#/operations/copilotgovernance_getSetting); absent from the docs.

notes.note: The casing split is not a documentation slip. Microsoft's own models declare these properties camelCase (`powerApps_AllowCodeApps`, `id`), while the running service returns PascalCase. Use the PascalCase spelling: it is the one `$select` matches.

The docs define one Value model reused for both the role-definition list and the role-assignment list. macroRegionId.description: Identifies the macro region. Its accepted values are chosen by the service and are not published: a client is expected to render whatever the response returns, using `displayName` and `dataResidencyNote`, rather than to know the set in advance.

notes.note: The value set is deliberately open. Microsoft's own SDK (`Microsoft.PowerPlatform.Management` 2.0.3503.299) types `MacroRegionId` as a bare string, while twelve lines away in the same generated file it emits `LocationSelectionMode` as a real enum with `Region` and `MacroRegion`. So this is a generator that does produce enums for closed sets and did not produce one here. Read with the shape of the object -- it carries its own `displayName` and `dataResidencyNote` -- the intent is that a client renders a picker without knowing any identifier. Choosing a macro region by a hardcoded id is working against the design.

Microsoft's own SDK (`Microsoft.PowerPlatform.Management` 2.0.3503.299) enumerates eleven values the published reference omits: `Internal_AI_BC`, `Internal_ISV_DataverseUserSync`, `Internal_AI_TemporaryCapacity`, `Internal_OmniChannelRecordRouting`, `Internal_OmniChannelVoice`, `Internal_OmniChannelLiveChat`, `Internal_OmniChannelDigitalMessaging`, `PowerPagesMigration_PortalAddOns_Authenticated`, `PowerPagesMigration_PortalAddOns_Anonymous`, `PowerPagesMigration_PortalLogins`, `PowerPagesMigration_PortalViews`. The `Internal_` prefix suggests they are not caller-selectable, but they can appear in a response.

**The envelope is `collection`, not the OData `value` used elsewhere on this host.** `/environmentmanagement/environments` returns `value`; this route and the per-environment operations list return `collection`. A client with one envelope reader will silently find nothing on one of them.

A first-party client's source comment describes the envelope as `{collection, continuationToken}`. A recorded response carrying all 20 locations had **no** `continuationToken` at all -- absent, not null, not empty. So either it appears only when a page is incomplete, which would match this API family's habit of omitting rather than nulling, or the comment describes an envelope the route does not use. Nobody has observed a truncated page, so it is not modelled here. The same comment also omits `hasFirstReleaseIslandAvailableForProvisioning`, which the recording does contain, so it is incomplete on a point that can be checked.

ThoughtProperties.description: The content of a reasoning step.

TriggerEvent.description: The event that started the run.

inputs.description: The trigger payload. Its shape is whatever the trigger's connector defines, so it is not modelled here. Large payloads are omitted and delivered through inputsLink instead.

requiresInlineApproval.description: Whether the run must pause for a person to approve this action before it executes.

ValidationProperties.description: Whether an action must be approved by a person before it runs.

WebApplicationFirewallStatus.description: How far a Power Pages website's web application firewall has got in being provisioned. `None` means no firewall; `Created` is the only state in which it is actually filtering. The two failure states are terminal — retry the enable or disable rather than waiting.

WhereClause.description: Filters rows by comparing `FieldName` against `Values` with `Operator`.

Operator.description: The comparison to apply, for example `eq`, `ne`, `contains` or `in`. The set of operators the service accepts is not enumerated by any source available here.

Values.description: The values to compare against. A single-element list is an equality test; several elements make it a set membership test.

Geo.description: A geography an ISV contract covers. The contract request carries a list of them.

GatewayError.description: The error the API gateway returns when it rejects a request before routing it, notably an unusable `api-version`. Nested `innererror` codes narrow the reason, and the innermost one is the machine-readable discriminator.

message.description: Human-readable text. For an api-version rejection it enumerates the accepted versions, which is often the only place that set is published.

GatewayInnerError.description: A narrowing error code, optionally nesting another. For an api-version rejection the presence of a second level distinguishes a version the gateway does not know at all from one it knows but this resource does not offer.

code.description: `ApiVersionUnsupported` at the outer level; a nested `ApiVersionUnsupportedForResource` means the version is valid somewhere but not here.
